Our actions being either <ns0:hi>Natural,</ns0:hi> as eating, drinking, sleeping, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Moral,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Spiritual.</ns0:hi> These powers are either <ns0:hi>Natural,</ns0:hi> which are in an ordinary course of Provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence bred with us, as the infant hath a power to eat, drink, sleep, cry, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Acquired,</ns0:hi> and that by imitation, or humane learning, as the child gets an habit of speaking, or a power to write, understand Languages, Arts, and Sciences. Or <ns0:hi>infused,</ns0:hi> and those are either <ns0:hi>meerly infused,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Faith, Love,</ns0:hi> and all ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bits truly spiritual are; and therefore called <ns0:hi>Graces</ns0:hi> or spiritual Gifts of the highest natures, or else such as are obtained by the use of means on our parts, but yet not without the influence of the holy Spirit of God; such are <ns0:hi>abilities</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>pray, preach,</ns0:hi> &c. There are some common powers, that is, such as those might have, who should never be saved, which might be <ns0:hi>meerly infused,</ns0:hi> and were extraordinary in those first Times of the Gospel; such as the Gift of <ns0:hi>Tongues, Prophecy, Healing,</ns0:hi> &c. These powers, espe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cially such as are not natural and common to all in an ordinary course of Providence, nor acquired meerly by imitation, or study, or the teaching of others, but infused either in whole, or in part, are those which the Apostle here calleth Gifts: and he <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>aith, there is a diversity of them; there was the Gift of <ns0:hi>Prophecy,</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Healing,</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Tongues,</ns0:hi> &c. but he tells them, this di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />versity of Gifts flowed all from one and the same Spirit, the Spirit was not diverse, though his influences were divers.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 12.6, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Eph. 4.11.</ns0:note> And there are differences of administra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions, but the same Lord <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">There are divers Offices or Ministries in the Church of God, one ministreth in the Office of an Elder, another in the Office of a Deacon, one in one service of the Church, another in another service, but there is but one Lord to whom they mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />inster; they all serve the great Lord of the Church, Jesus Christ, though in divers Orders, and places of Ministration.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Eph. 1.23.</ns0:note> which worketh all in all <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Operations</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ministrations</ns0:hi> both differ from <ns0:hi>Gifts,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>Habits: Habits</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Powers,</ns0:hi> by which men performed ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly Offices in the Church, or wrought Miracles, are called <ns0:hi>Gifts.</ns0:hi> The Acts or exercise of these Powers are called <ns0:hi>Ministrations</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Operations.</ns0:hi> These latter differ one from another, as the former signifie standing and continuing Acts in the Church; <ns0:hi>Operations,</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, rather signifies <ns0:hi>miraculous effects,</ns0:hi> such as <ns0:hi>healing</ns0:hi> the sick, without the application of ordinary means, <ns0:hi>speaking with divers Tongues,</ns0:hi> &c. The Apostle tells them, That as there was a diversity of <ns0:hi>Gifts,</ns0:hi> or Powers, and a diversity of Acts in the constant Service of the Church, by which men ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ercised those Gifts or Powers they had in the performance of them: So there were diversities of Operations, by which men used those extraordinary <ns0:hi>Gifts</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Powers,</ns0:hi> which God gave some in the first plantation of the Church, for the sake of such as be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved not. But it was the same God that wrought them all, and in all<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> though all did not do, or could not do the same things.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 But the manifestation of the Spirit <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">He here calleth Gifts, the <ns0:hi>manifestation of the Spirit,</ns0:hi> partly to let them know, that these powers flowed from the holy Spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rit apparently, they having no such powers while they were Heathens, and carried after dumb Idols, as they were led; and partly to let all know, that these gifts and powers were evident proofs both of Christs Ascension, and of the Promise of the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, and of Christ in sending the holy Spirit, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.4. and 16.7, 8. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 4.8.</ns0:note> is given to every man to profit withal <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">These gifts he tells them were given to <ns0:hi>every one,</ns0:hi> where <ns0:hi>every</ns0:hi> signifieth <ns0:hi>each one</ns0:hi>; for the same gifts or powers were not given to all, but to those to whom they were given, they were given not to puff them up, or to give them matter to boast of, but to do good withal to the Church of Christ. No man hath any power or gift given him of God, ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther for his own hurt, or the hurt of others<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but only for his own good, and the good of others.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 For to one is given by the Spirit, the word of wisdom <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">There are different apprehensions as to the particular <ns0:hi>Gifts</ns0:hi> here enumerated, and it is no wonder these extraordinary Gifts being ceased, if we be now at a loss to determine what is to be understood by the terms whereby they are expressed. Some by the <ns0:hi>word of Wisdom</ns0:hi> here understand a faculty to deliver grave Sentences: others, an ability to open the deep Mysteries of Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ligion: others, a <ns0:hi>singular Knowledge</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>spiritual things,</ns0:hi> joined with a great authority, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> others, an ability to explain the deep Wisdom of God. But it is most probable, that he mean<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth by it what we ordinarily understand by Wisdom, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>faculty</ns0:hi> from a good judgment of the circumstances of actions, to do them at the best time, and in the best manner wherein they may be serviceable to their ends.</ns0:note>, to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">It is as uncertain, whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther by the <ns0:hi>word of Knowledge</ns0:hi> he meaneth a capacity to com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prehend things in our knowledge, or to communicate it to o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers, or the actual communication of it by preaching, which was the work of the Pastors and Teachers, or the Prophetical knowledge of future contingencies, or an ability to speak of spiritual things Doctrinally, without any great faculty of apply<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 To another faith by the same Spirit <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">To another, he saith, is given <ns0:hi>Faith.</ns0:hi> By which cannot be understood that <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> which is common to all Christians, for he is speaking of such gifts as were given to some Christians, not to all; he must therefore mean, either a <ns0:hi>Faith of Miracles,</ns0:hi> that is, a perswasion that God would work a Miracle in this or that case, or a great knowledge in the matters of Faith; or a great confidence and boldness in the discharge of their Office.</ns0:note>: to a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nother the gifts of healing by the same Spirit <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">To another <ns0:hi>the gift of Healing,</ns0:hi> of healing diseases miraculously, without the application of ordinary rational Medicines.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 To another the working of miracles <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">To another the <ns0:hi>working of Miracles,</ns0:hi> of other sorts<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> such as the inflicting punishments on sinners, casting out Devils, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, to a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nother prophecy <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">To another <ns0:hi>Prophecy,</ns0:hi> which in the general signifieth the Reve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lation of the Will of God, whether by the foretelling future contingencies, or opening the Scriptures by preaching or <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>each<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing.</ns0:note>, to another discerning of spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rits <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">To another <ns0:hi>discerning of Spirits.</ns0:hi> A power wherein God, for the further authority and credit of his Gospel in the primitive Times, communicated to some men something of his own Prerogative to discern mens inward thoughts and hearts, and to make up a judgment of their truth and sincerity, or con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trariwise of their falshood and hypocrisie.</ns0:note>, to another <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 2.4.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>divers</ns0:hi> kinds of tongues <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">To another <ns0:hi>di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vers kinds of Tongues,</ns0:hi> that is, a power to discourse with men in their several Languages, as we read in <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 2.8.</ns0:note>, to a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nother the interpretation of tongues <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">To another the <ns0:hi>Interpretation of Tongues.</ns0:hi> This is made a diverse gift from an ability to speak with divers Tongues, possibly some of those that spake with divers Tongues could not interpret what they said.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 But all these worketh that one and the self same Spirit, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 7.7. 2 Cor. 10.13.</ns0:note> dividing to every one severally, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 3.8. Heb. 2.4.</ns0:note> as he will <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Though the Spirit of God be but one, from whom these several powers and abilities flow; yet he doth not give all this variety of gifts to all Christians, but one to this man, another to another, as the same holy Spirit pleaseth for the glory of God, or the good of the Church.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 For as <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 12.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Eph. 4.4.16.</ns0:note> the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> Christ <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">For as it is in the Body natural, the integral parts, or members of it, are many, yet the body is but one: so it is in the spiritual Body, the Church, which is that mystical Body of which Christ is the Head. The Members of the Church may be many, and there may be in several Members of the Church a diversity of <ns0:hi>Gifts,</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Ministrations</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Operations,</ns0:hi> yet the Church is but one, yea Christ and the Church make up but one mysti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cal Body, of which he is the Head, and they are the Members, and therefore the several Members having several gifts, or seve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral offices, or several powers and operations, had no reason for their difference in such gifts or powers or offi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>es to envy one another, or to despise each other, or glory over one another; for they were but one Body, and had all the same Head, though they had from the same Spirit divers abilities, offices, and powers for several Operations.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:452" />13 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 6.5.</ns0:note> by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gal. 3.28. Eph. 2.13, 14, 16. Col. 3.11.</ns0:note> whether <ns0:hi>we be</ns0:hi> Jews or <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>Greeks.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Gentiles, whether <ns0:hi>we be</ns0:hi> bond or free <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The Apostle proveth the Oneness of the Church, as the Body of Christ, from the same Sacraments of the New Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment instituted for all Christians, and wherein they jointly par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />take. He saith, we are <ns0:hi>baptized into one body,</ns0:hi> by which he must mean the universal Church, for Christ is the Head of that; pa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>icular Churches are but parts of that Church, of which Christ is the Head. Let men be of what Nation they will, whether Jews or Gentiles, turning to the Christian Religion, and of what condition they will, when they are baptized they are by it made Members of that one Body, of which Christ is the Head; though for the more convenient administration of, and participation in the Ordinances, they are divided into smaller Societies, which also have the denomination of Churches, as the smallest drop of water may be called water, though there be but one Element of Water.</ns0:note>: and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 6.63.</ns0:note> have been all made to drink into one Spirit <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">And, saith the Apostle, <ns0:hi>We have been all made to drink into one Spirit,</ns0:hi> which some interpret as if it were, we have all drank of one Spirit, that is, been made partakers of one Spirit, whose benefits are sometimes set out under the notion of water, <ns0:hi>living water, Ioh.</ns0:hi> 4.14. and 7.38, 39. and so in the Old Testament, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 12.3. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 47. But many others rather chuse to interpret drinking in this place, of <ns0:hi>drinking</ns0:hi> at the Table of the Lord, partaking of that whole Action being set out here by one particular act there perform<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed. This is probable, considering that the Apostle, in the for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mer part of the verse, had been speaking of the other Sacra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of the Gospel, and that he speaking of the Lords Supper, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 10.17. had used this expression, <ns0:hi>For we being many, are one bread and one body.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 For the body is not one member, but ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">As the natural Body is <ns0:hi>Totum integrale,</ns0:hi> a Whole consisting of many members; so the Body spiritual, the mystical Body of Christ is not made up of one single Member, but of many Members.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 If the foot shall say, Because I am not the hand, I am not of the body: is it therefore not of the body?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And if the ear shall say, Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body: is it therefore not of the body? <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">It should seem by these expressions, that one great cause of those divisions, which the Apostle had charged the Church of <ns0:hi>Corinth</ns0:hi> with, was their difference in <ns0:hi>Gifts, Ministrations,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Operations</ns0:hi>; which was to that degree, that either those who were higher in Gifts and Ministrations, and more famous for their miraculous Operations, despised and vilified those that were inferiour to them; or those who were lower in Gifts, or in their stations in the Church, or their power to work Miracles, would not owne themselves Members of the Church at <ns0:hi>Corinth,</ns0:hi> because they were in those low, and inferiour orders and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />grees. The Apostle argueth the unreasonableness of this, by a further comparing of the natural with the spiritual mystical Bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dy, the Church<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and sheweth, it was altogether as unreasona<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble, for men to disclaim the Church, and their relation to it, because they had not the most eminent gifts, or were not in the most eminent places and Offices; as for the foot to say, It was not of the body, because it was not the hand; or for the ear to say, It was not of the body, because it was not the eye.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 If the whole body <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> an eye, where <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> the hearing? If the whole body <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> hearing, where <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> the smelling? <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">There are several actions to be performed by the body of a man, either for the support and the upholding of it in life, or for the accommodation of it while it lives; <ns0:hi>Seeing, Hearing,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Smelling</ns0:hi> (which are the three actions here mentioned) are not indeed necessary for the upholding of life, but they are highly useful for a mans better being, and the accommodation of bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dily life; therefore there is need of a variety of bodily mem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bers, Organs, or Instruments of Sight, as well as of Hearing, and Organs of Smelling, as well as Hearing; the wise God hath created no member of mans body in vain, each one hath its use in order to the being or well being of the body: So it is in the Church of God, as the Apostle, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 26. argueth; but he goe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>h yet further on, first in his comparison of the natural, and my<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stical Body.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The infinitely wise God, who hath made the body of man, and ordered all the members of the body for several uses and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ffic<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s, either for the upholding, or accommodating the life of man, hath likewise appointed the order in the body, in which every member shall stand; that the head should be uppermost for the better guidance of the whole body; the feet lowermost to tread upon the earth, and to bear the weight of the whole body: and none must repine at the Wisdom of God, which hath not only created mans body, (consisting of a variety of members) but also appointed every member its place, and there setreth it, that it cannot shift its station or office.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And if they were all one member, where <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> the body? <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The body is a Whole consisting of many members, it could not therefore be a body, if there were but only one member. Or how could the body perform the several actions necessary either for the being, or the well being of it, if it consisted but of one member?</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 But now <ns0:hi>are they</ns0:hi> many members, yet but one body <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The multiplicity of members, having several uses and offi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces for the service of the whole body, do not make a multipli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />city of bodies, the body still is but one.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">He names two of the most noble and useful members of the body, the <ns0:hi>Head</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Eye,</ns0:hi> which yet cannot tell the hands or the feet, they have no need of them: the wise God having created nothing in vain, but made every member in the body of a man for use, as to the whole, so to the several parts of the body, the hand is useful to the eye, and the feet are of use to the head. The application of this similitude, which the Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stle so much inlargeth upon, we shall have <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 26, 27, &c.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 Nay much more those members of the bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dy, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">By <ns0:hi>feeble</ns0:hi> the Apostle here doth not only mean <ns0:hi>most weak,</ns0:hi> but which seem to us most abject and contemptible, in which sense the word is used 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 12.10. such are the belly and the entrails; the Eye also is a feeble member, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> yet these parts are most necessary for the use of the body, being such without the use of which the body cannot live.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 And those <ns0:hi>members</ns0:hi> of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stow more abundant honour, and our uncomely <ns0:hi>parts</ns0:hi> have more abundant comeliness <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">All know what those parts of the body are, which are com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monly judged <ns0:hi>less honourable</ns0:hi> and less comely, upon these we bestow more abundant honour and comeliness, by hiding them and covering them, that they are not, as the <ns0:hi>hands</ns0:hi> and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> and <ns0:hi>head</ns0:hi> (which we esteem more honourable parts of the bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dy) exposed to the publick view of those with whom we <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 For our comely <ns0:hi>parts</ns0:hi> have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven more abundant honour to that <ns0:hi>part</ns0:hi> which lacked <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">God hath in the Wisdom of his Providence so ordered it, that as we have some parts of our body, which are judged un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />comely, and not for those noble uses that others are; so we have other parts that are, for use, more noble, yet in common repute more ignoble and uncomely: and the same wise God hath so builded the body of man, as of both these to make <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> temperament so, as they all concur in the composition of the same body, and more abundant honour in covering and cloath<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing them, is given to those parts, that in the judgment of men, seemed most to lack honour, that their uncomeliness might by some artificial means be taken away.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 That there should be no <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>divis<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> schism in the bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dy, but <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> the members should have the same care one for another <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">By <ns0:hi>Schism</ns0:hi> is here meant division, and that also must be expounded figuratively, and it is expounded in the next words, that the members should take the same care one for another. That though the members differ in honour and office, yet they might mutually take care for each other, as if they were all in an equal degree of honour.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it, or one member be honou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red, all the members rejoice with it <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">From this union of the members in the body natural of all the members proceedeth a natural Sympathy, that if one mem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ber suffereth, all are afflicted, and ready to contribute to the relief and help each of other; and likewise the honour that is reflected on the body, is reflected on all the par<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

               <ns0:p n="28">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:452" />28 And God hath set some in the church, first apostles <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The Apostle, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 4.11. seemeth to make a different enu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />meration, there he saith, <ns0:hi>And he gave some Apostles, and some Prophets, and some Evangelists, and some Pastors and Teachers.</ns0:hi> He mentioneth here only three of those there mentioned, <ns0:hi>viz. Apostles, Prophets, Teachers.</ns0:hi> He reckoneth up here <ns0:hi>Evangelists,</ns0:hi> whom he doth not there mention. He here first mentioneth <ns0:hi>Apostles,</ns0:hi> by whom he meaneth those Servants of God who were <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ent out by Christ to lay the first foundations of the Gospel-Church, and upon whom an universal care lay over all the Churches of Christ, having not only a power in all places, to preach and administer the Sacraments, but to give Rules of Or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der, and direct in matters of Government, though particular Churches had a power of Government within themselves (other<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wise the Apostle would not have blamed this Church, for not casting out the incestuous person.)</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Eph. 2.20.</ns0:note> secondarily prophets <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> signifies per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons (as I have before noted) that revealed the Mind and Will of God to people, whether it were by an extraordinary impulse and Revelation, or in an ordinary course of Teaching; whether they revealed things to come, or opened the Mind and Will of God already revealed. But in this Text, and in <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 4.11. <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> seem to signifie, either such as from the Spirit of God, foretold future contingencies (such was <ns0:hi>Agabus,</ns0:hi> of whom we read in the <ns0:hi>Acts of the Apostles,</ns0:hi> and others in the Primitive Church) or else such as interpreted Scripture by extraordinary <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>d immediate <ns0:hi>Revelation.</ns0:hi> Some think, that <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> signifie the <ns0:hi>ordinary Pastors</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Churches</ns0:hi>; but they seem rather t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> be comprehended under the next term of <ns0:hi>Teachers,</ns0:hi> unless we had bet<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>er grounds, than we have, to distinguish betwixt <ns0:hi>Pastors</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Teachers,</ns0:hi> making the work of the Teacher to speak by way of Doctrine and Explication, and the work of the Pastor to speak practically.</ns0:note>, thirdly tea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chers <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Thirdly, <ns0:hi>Teachers:</ns0:hi> Some by these under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand Governours of Schools; others, such Ministers, whose work was only to expound the Scriptures, or the Mysteries of Salvation: but the Apostle in this Enumeration (which is the largest we have in Scripture) not mentioning <ns0:hi>Pastors</ns0:hi>; it seem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth to me that he means the fixed and ordinary Ministers of Churches, or the Elders, whom the Apostles left i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> every City, which by their Ministry had received the Gospel.</ns0:note>, after that miracles <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">After that such as he impowered to work miraculous Operations, and those of more remarkable nature, for otherwise the <ns0:hi>healings</ns0:hi> next mentioned, come under that notion also.</ns0:note>, then gifts of heal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Then such persons as he gave a power to in an extraordinary way to he<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>l the sick.</ns0:note>, helps <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Who the Apostle means by <ns0:hi>Helps,</ns0:hi> and</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 12.8. 1 Tim. 5.17. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 13.17, 24.</ns0:note> governments <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">by <ns0:hi>Governments,</ns0:hi> is very hard to determine. Certain it is, that he doth not mean the Civil Magistrates; for the time was not yet come for <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> to be <ns0:hi>nursing Fathers,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Queens nursing Mothers</ns0:hi> to the Gospel-Church. But whether he meaneth <ns0:hi>Deacons,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Widows,</ns0:hi> elsewhere mentioned, as helpful in the case of the Poor, or some that assisted the Pastors in the Government of the Church, or some that were extraordinary helps to the Apostles in the first Plantation of the Church, is very hard to determine.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> diversities of tongues <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Such as spake with divers Tongues, that faculty being a gift, as we heard before, not given to all, but to some in the Primi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ti<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e Church The Apostle, by this Enumeration, sheweth what he meant by those diversities of Gifts, differences of Administrations, and diversities of Operations, of which he spake in <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4, 5, 6.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 <ns0:hi>Are</ns0:hi> all apostles? <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> all prophets? <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> all teachers? <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> all workers of <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>powers.</ns0:hi>
